tagline: Sync Jira epics to Notion project pages and document sprint retros automatically
metaTitle: Jira + Notion Integration: Notion Pages from Jira Epics
metaDescription: Scaffold Notion project pages from Jira epics and show live story status in Notion specs. GAIA links tickets and docs. See the setup steps.
intro:
Jira and Notion serve different but complementary roles in a product engineering organization. Jira tracks the executable: stories, bugs, sprints, and releases. Notion holds the interpretive: specs, ADRs, retros, and project narratives. The problem is that the two rarely stay in sync. Sprint retro templates sit empty while the data already exists in the sprint. Epic docs go stale while the actual work evolves.

GAIA keeps both synchronized without requiring anyone to manually copy data between them. When an epic is created, GAIA scaffolds a project page with the epic context. When a sprint ends, GAIA populates the retro template with the sprint data. When an epic is marked complete, the page reflects the final state.

This integration is most impactful for product engineering teams that invest in documentation quality and want their docs to always reflect what is actually happening in the tracked work rather than representing a snapshot from the last time someone remembered to update them.

useCases.title: Scaffold Notion project pages from Jira epics
useCases.description: When a new epic is created, GAIA creates a corresponding project page pre-populated with the epic name, description, acceptance criteria, and a linked table of child stories so the team has a documentation home for the feature from day one.

useCases.title: Auto-populate sprint retrospective templates
useCases.description: At the end of each sprint, GAIA fills the team's retro template with sprint metrics, stories completed, velocity, carry-over, and bugs closed, so the retrospective meeting can focus on insights rather than data gathering.

useCases.title: Embed live Jira story status in specs
useCases.description: GAIA maintains a synchronized table in each epic page showing the current status of all linked stories. Product managers and designers can see engineering progress directly in the spec document without accessing Jira.

useCases.title: Create epics from Notion product briefs
useCases.description: When a product brief is tagged Ready for Engineering, GAIA creates an epic and its child stories from the brief's requirements section, linking each created item back to the source document.

useCases.title: Update release notes when versions ship
useCases.description: When a version or release is marked as released, GAIA appends the included stories and bug fixes to the team's release notes page in a formatted, user-facing changelog entry.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Notion to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA with your project and workspace. Map Jira projects to Notion databases or page hierarchies during setup.

howItWorks.step: Configure sync rules and template mappings
howItWorks.description: Specify which events trigger page creation or updates, which page templates should be used for epics and retros, and how issue fields should map to page properties.
GAIA monitors both sides and applies updates automatically. Pages reflect the current state of the work, and epics can be seeded from product briefs.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync Jira subtasks to Notion or only epics and stories?
faqs.answer: GAIA supports configurable depth. You can sync only epics, epics and stories, or the full epic-story-subtask hierarchy. Most teams sync epics and stories to keep the docs at a strategic level while leaving tactical subtask details in the ticket tracker.

faqs.question: Will GAIA overwrite content I write manually in a page?
faqs.answer: GAIA writes only to dedicated sections and database properties it manages. Free-form content you add to a page is never modified. It uses clearly marked blocks and properties to separate its automated content from your manual additions.

faqs.question: Does GAIA support Service Management projects as well as Software projects?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both project types are supported. For service management projects, GAIA can sync incident and request data to knowledge base pages and post-mortem templates.
